summary.name: SRE@Xero: Managing Incidents Part I
summary.one_liner: A Xero SRE blog post describing how the team detects production incidents, turns manual issue reports into automated alerts, and manages on-call configuration as code.
use_cases: Designing an alerting pipeline for production issues
Writing alert templates that tell on-call engineers what broke and how to fix it
Letting other teams report incidents through a form that feeds automated alerts
Managing many on-call teams and rotations through Git-based configuration
Learning how an SRE team structures incident intake
summary.what_it_does: The post explains Xero's SRE incident workflow starting from detection. Most production issues are caught by monitoring and sent through an automated alerting pipeline to the right engineer. Manual reports from other teams are converted into the same kind of automated alert via an online form that asks for a summary, affected URL, affected users, location, start time and who is working on it. The author also describes an "on-call as code" system where teams change on-call configuration through Git, and a CI job runs a Rake task to synchronise it with a third-party on-call management system. The post is the first in a series and says later posts will cover ChatOps for resolution.
notable: On-call as code: on-call configuration lives in Git and is synced to the on-call system by CI, with lint checks such as one administrator per team
Manual incident reports are turned into the same automated alerts as monitoring-detected issues
Covers over 20 on-call teams and SRE cover layers
Part I of a series; ChatOps incident handling is covered in a later post
caveats: Describes internal Xero tooling, not a publicly available product
Specific third-party on-call system is not named on the page
Part I only; the ChatOps and tooling details are in later posts
